title: Foundations: Pop Hits - The Complete Guide
summary: What Pop Hits is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Pop Hits songs: Pop hits are engineered joy: three minutes, a hook in the first 30 seconds, and a chorus built for maximum singalong. The craft is invisible; the chorus is inevitable.

History: From Brill Building songwriters (1960s) through ABBA, Michael Jackson's Thriller (1982), and Max Martin's 1990s–2000s hit factory, pop has been refined into a science of hooks.

How the songs work: Pop Hits favors the keys of C, G, D, F. Common forms include Verse–pre-chorus–chorus, post-chorus hook; The chorus arrives before 60 seconds. Players should master the post-chorus: a wordless hook after the chorus first, then max martin's melodic math: repetition with variation. Piano-pop keys; guitarists adapt.

title: Billie Jean - Pop Hits Song Study
summary: Harmonic blueprint and playing guide for Billie Jean by Michael Jackson (1982).
body:
Billie Jean — Michael Jackson, 1982. The bassline that changed pop.

HARMONIC BLUEPRINT (study chart, key of D):
Dm | G | C | Am

This study chart uses the 'Millennial ii–V–I–vi' progression, the Pop Hits workhorse, to map how songs like this move. Form: verse–pre-chorus–chorus, post-chorus hook. Listen for key change for the final chorus — it is the fingerprint of the style.

TO PLAY IT: set your tempo to the Pop Hits pocket, voice the chords cleanly, and let key change for the final chorus. Piano-pop keys; guitarists adapt. (Song facts: title/artist/year are documented public records; the chart is an original study arrangement.)
